problem_structuring.description: Assesses whether the student breaks the business problem into a clear and logical framework.

criteria.1: No clear framework or only an uncategorised list.
criteria.2: Some structure is present, but categories are weak, generic or not MECE.
criteria.3: Clear structure with relevant categories, but limited prioritisation or measurable detail.
criteria.4: Clear, MECE, case-specific and prioritised framework with relevant data points.

business_logic.description: Assesses whether the student connects their reasoning to the business objective of the case.

criteria.1: Reasoning is disconnected from the business problem.
criteria.2: Shows partial understanding but often expands or complicates the problem unnecessarily.
criteria.3: Understands the problem and links some insights back to the main issue.
criteria.4: Maintains strong focus on the business objective and consistently drives toward a solution.

assumptions_and_evidence.description: Assesses whether the student justifies assumptions and supports claims with evidence from the case.

criteria.1: Makes claims without justification or evidence.
criteria.2: Provides some assumptions but they are vague, unsupported or not clearly explained.
criteria.3: Uses relevant assumptions and evidence, but not consistently or deeply.
criteria.4: Clearly states, justifies and connects assumptions to case evidence and business implications.

communication.description: Assesses whether the student communicates clearly, concisely and in an interview-appropriate way.

criteria.1: Unclear, hard to follow or lacks confidence.
criteria.2: Some clear points, but often rambling or unstructured.
criteria.3: Mostly clear and concise, but could improve prioritisation or synthesis.
criteria.4: Clear, confident, concise and structured communication using logical points.
